cards.text: The writer of Hebrews has just urged his readers to imitate those who inherit what God has promised (Hebrews 6:12). So he points to Abraham, the man who left home when God called him, without knowing where he was going (Hebrews 11:8). God made Abraham a promise, and He backed it up with an oath.

cards.question: When God swore His oath to Abraham, He swore by ___.

cards.text: Why Himself? Because God had no one greater to swear by. When you're at the very top, there's nobody left to call as a witness.

cards.question: So what did God swear He would do for Abraham?

answers.text: Bless him and give him many descendants
Make him a priest in a great temple
Give him silver and gold all his life

cards.text: Then came the part NOBODY likes, baker: the waiting. Trust me, I did YEARS in a junk drawer, and nobody even gave me a promise.

cards.question: Abraham, after waiting ___, obtained the promise.

cards.text: Now the writer turns to people: when they make an oath, they swear by someone greater than themselves. Nobody in history ever said, "I swear on my coworker Kevin."

cards.question: When people swear by someone greater than themselves, what does their oath do?

cards.text: Now bring that back to God. He wanted to make something very clear to the heirs of the promise, so He guaranteed it with an oath.

cards.question: With His oath, God wanted to make the ___ nature of His purpose very clear to the heirs of the promise.

cards.text: So the writer points to two unchangeable things. Me? When I promise a batch in ten minutes, that means ten, maybe twenty, maybe THURSDAY.

cards.question: In these two unchangeable things, it is impossible for God to ___.
For those who have fled to take hold of the hope set before them, these two unchangeable things bring strong encouragement.

cards.text: Then the writer gives this hope a picture: an anchor for the soul. The closest thing I've got is this gold base, and it STILL lets me dive face-first into the chocolate chips.

cards.question: An anchor keeps a ship from drifting. How does the writer describe this hope that anchors the soul?

cards.text: The writer says this anchor of hope enters the inner sanctuary, behind the curtain. And here's what gets me every time: somebody has already gone in there ahead of us, on our behalf.

cards.question: Who has already entered behind the curtain ahead of us, on our behalf?

cards.text: And Jesus has become a high priest in the order of Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of God Most High, who blessed Abraham (Genesis 14:18-19).

cards.question: Jesus has become a high priest in the order of Melchizedek, but only for a set time.
